analysis: This batch has only documentation changes: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/overlapped-weight-verification.md, lines 1-9) and one paragraph in docs/reference/configuration.md (head lines 621-625). No source code is included, so no control change can be verified directly. The documents describe a reader thread that stays one 4 MiB chunk ahead of SHA-256, using a second page-aligned buffer (OverlappedFileDigest). They state that digests are unchanged, that weights still bypass the file cache via F_NOCACHE, and that PageCache.drop still runs after the read. The docs make no claim that weakens verification: the full hash is still computed, the fallback readers remain, and the pre/post-load fresh hashes for SSD prefix caching are retained. These hashes underpin weight-substitution defenses (T-012, T-027) and the cache-binding mitigation in T-041, which relies on a verified weightHash. The remaining questions sit in the unprovided implementation, which is outside this batch. First, whether the reader thread and hasher are correctly synchronized, with no TOCTOU between chunk read and hash and no short-read or error swallowing that could yield a wrong or partial digest accepted as verified. Second, whether read errors on the reader thread propagate as failures rather than as a truncated digest. Third, whether the buffers hold weight data only, which is not sensitive plaintext of consumer prompts. The docs do not establish any of these properties, so a later pass that sees the WeightHasher/OverlappedFileDigest code should check them. The documentation does not create a regression or invalidate a threat-model assumption.
